description: Three drum voices — a sine kick, a snare of sine and filtered noise, and a hat of filtered square and noise — each played by an envelope patched into it rather than by any clock of its own

params.text: Sets the level of the kick, 0 to 1
Sets the pitch of the kick oscillator, 24Hz to 500Hz
Sets how far the kick envelope sweeps its oscillator, up to twenty octaves at the top of its travel
Drives the kick into a saturator, leaving it alone at the bottom of its travel and pushing it five times over at the top
Sets the level of the snare, 0 to 1
Sets the pitch of the snare body, 100Hz to 300Hz
Sets the centre of the band-pass on the snare noise, adding up to 5000Hz above five times the body pitch
Crossfades the snare between its sine body and its filtered noise, body alone at the bottom of its travel and noise alone at the top
Sets the level of the hats, 0 to 1
Sets the pitch of the hats square wave, 1000Hz at the bottom of its travel to 5500Hz at the top, and opens the filter above it by the same amount
Sets how much filtered noise is added to the hats and how sharply they die away: at the bottom of its travel no noise and the fastest fall, at the top most noise and the slowest
Sets how hard the kick accent voltage pulls the snare down, 0 to 1; at the top a third of ten volts on the accent jack is enough to silence it

inputs.text: The envelope that plays the kick: its square sets the pitch sweep and its square root the level, so 0V is silence and 10V a full hit
Multiplies the kick's level, 0V silencing it and 10V leaving it at full; the duck control is driven from this jack as well
Added to the kick TUNE knob, one volt per octave; the pitch is held between 24Hz and 500Hz
Added to the kick FM knob, two octaves of sweep per volt; the total is held between none and twenty octaves
Added to the kick PUNCH knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
The envelope that plays the snare: its square root sets the level, so 0V is silence and 10V a full hit, and it also opens the noise filter by up to 2000Hz
Added to the snare N.MIX knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
The envelope that plays the hats: 0V is silence and 10V a full hit, raised to a power the hats DECAY knob sets
Added to the hats DECAY knob, a tenth of its travel per volt; the total is held between the two ends of it
A signal mixed into both mix outputs after the duck is applied to it, so it ducks with the snare

outputs.text: The kick alone, quantised to about ten bits
The snare alone, quantised to about ten bits
The hats alone, quantised to about ten bits
The three voices and the external input added, then soft-limited above 5V
The three voices and the external input added, with the hats delayed by 20ms so the pair spreads, then soft-limited above 5V

notes: this module has no sequencer and no clock jack. Nothing sounds until an envelope or gate is patched into one of the three ENV jacks.
the kick also needs a voltage at its accent jack before it can be heard at all, however hard its envelope is driven.
the duck control is driven by the kick accent voltage, not by the kick envelope, and it pulls down the snare and the external input in full and the hats by a fifth.
